reflections.title: "Be Strong and Very Courageous"

reflect.text: God cares deeply about what is happening inside our hearts. When we are weighed down by doubt or fear, He does not shrug it off as a small thing. He wants us to bring our heavy thoughts straight to Him. As Charles Spurgeon reminds us, our discouragement can spread to others, because "one downcast believer makes twenty souls sad." When we meet life's difficulties with cheerfulness and hope, we bring honor to God and guard ourselves against the enemy.

True courage is closely tied to how we handle God's word. The Lord called Joshua to be careful and obey everything written in the law, without turning to the right or to the left. We cannot simply pick and choose the parts of God's commands that seem easy or pleasant. We are called to follow His path with a steady, wholehearted trust. True spiritual success comes when we listen to God carefully and walk in His ways each day.

questions: In what areas of your life have you let fear or doubt take root lately?
Is there an instruction in God's word that you find hard to obey with your whole heart?
reflections.prayer: Lord, help us to bring our hidden fears and doubts to You instead of carrying them alone. Fill our hearts with gladness and courage so we can encourage those around us. Give us the desire and strength to obey all Your commands with a steady, faithful spirit. Amen.

reflections.title: "Do Not Be Afraid"

reflect.text: When God commanded Joshua not to be terrified, He was not ignoring Joshua's human weakness. Big changes in life are often intimidating, especially when one season ends and an unfamiliar road begins. We may need time to grieve what we have left behind while facing the fear of what lies ahead. Stepping forward into God's promises means walking forward before we know how everything will turn out.

God does not hand us a complete map of the future, nor does He promise an easy path with no hardship. Instead, He gives us something far better: the guarantee of His constant presence. He measures our lives not by worldly success, but by our quiet faithfulness. Courage does not mean having all the answers today. It simply means taking one obedient step at a time, confident that God is with us wherever we go.

questions: What unknown situation or new chapter is causing you anxiety right now?
What is one small step of obedience you can take today while trusting God with tomorrow?
reflections.prayer: Father, thank You for understanding our weakness when changes make us feel afraid. Remind us that You never ask us to walk alone. Help us to take each step in simple obedience, resting in Your faithful presence wherever we go. Amen.

D6.work: Stepping Forward in Faith as One Chapter Comes to a Close

reflections.title: Claiming What God Has Given

reflect.text: God had already promised the land to Israel, yet they still had to cross over and set their feet upon it. F. B. Meyer notes that the gift belonged to them, but it still had to be claimed inch by inch. In the same way, God has blessed us with every spiritual gift in Christ. He gives us peace, wisdom, and life, but we must step out in faith and take hold of what He has freely provided.

We find the spiritual energy to take those steps by feeding on God's word day and night. His truth nourishes our inner life and shows us what is ours through the cross of Christ. Even when we face daunting tasks or human friends let us down, the Lord of Hosts remains at our side. Because He will never fail or abandon us, our hearts can rest safely in His unchanging faithfulness.

questions: What spiritual promise from God do you need to actively claim by faith today?
How can you make more time each day to feed your soul on the scriptures?
reflections.prayer: Gracious God, thank You for every spiritual blessing You have given us in Christ. Feed our souls with Your truth so our faith remains strong and active. Teach us to step forward boldly, trusting that You will never fail or forsake us. Amen.
